key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence degradation of metal halide perovskites from early time-series data, enabling faster stability assessment.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable screening tool for perovskite solar-cell materials, reducing the need for lengthy accelerated-aging experiments while preserving interpretability.
method: Collected 167 perovskite samples spanning different compositions and crystallinities under heat and light stress.
Featurized more than 86,000 photoluminescence spectra with a physics-informed representation.
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL intensity for unseen samples and extracted stability descriptors from the physics-based features.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on a diverse dataset of 167 materials and outperformed baseline benchmarks while generalizing across material groups.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of the training dataset, so extrapolation to new perovskite chemistries or stress conditions should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
